guideTitle: 6 Best Book Lights for Comfortable Reading (2026)
metaDescription: Six rechargeable book lights compared on color temperature, brightness range and battery life, from amber night lights to clip on and neck styles.
introParagraphs: A good book light puts a small, steady pool of light on the page and leaves the rest of the room dark. The six picks here are all rechargeable and vary mainly in color range, dimming and form. The Amber Light + is the warmest at 1600K with three fixed levels of 20, 40 and 80 lumens, the DEWENWILS sits at 1800K, and the Gritin neck light offers four color temperatures with a 30 minute timer. In between, the 86lux gives stepless dimming from 10 to 100 percent and the HEMONNKAM has five brightness levels on a 500 mAh battery.

We evaluated each light based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at how much control you get over color and brightness, how long it runs, and how comfortably it clips on or hangs around the neck. Warm amber in the 1800K to 3200K range is generally recommended for bedtime reading, while 5000K to 6000K suits focused daytime work, so a light that covers both ranges is more flexible. The Gritin 19 LED horizontal head covers 1800K, 3400K and 6000K, which makes it the most versatile single clip light here.

For close up page reading, roughly 15 to 50 lumens is usually enough, and very high output only adds glare on white paper. That is why beam quality, flicker free output and easy dimming matter more than the biggest number on the box. We rank the picks by how well they balance warm light, simple controls and dependable battery life.

products.name: Gritin 19 LED Rechargeable Book Light
products.description:
The Gritin 19 LED is the most versatile clip light in this group. Its horizontal head spreads light across a wider area than a round spot, which helps when you read a full page or a two page spread. You get three color temperatures, from amber 1800K for bedtime through mixed 3400K to white 6000K for daytime, plus five brightness levels with a memory function.

The tradeoff is that more modes mean more button presses, and the light shows its controls in the dark only after you learn them. A 360 degree bendable gooseneck makes aiming easy, though a long gooseneck can droop on a heavy hardcover. The wide head is also bulkier than a compact bookmark style light.

Setup is just a clip and a USB charge, and the light folds small for a bag. Compared with the DEWENWILS it offers three colors instead of one, and against the Amber Light + it gives a wider head with more brightness steps. It is the safe all around pick when one light needs to serve both night and day.
products.bestFor: Readers who want amber for night and white for day in a single clip light.
pros: Wide horizontal head lights a full page
360 degree gooseneck is easy to aim
cons: More modes mean more button presses to learn
Wide head is bulkier than a bookmark style light

products.name: 86lux Rechargeable Clip On LED Book Light

specList.label: Dimming
specList.value: Presets 10, 50 and 100 percent or smooth 10 to 100 percent

products.description:
The 86lux is the pick for readers who like to fine tune their light. It gives both preset brightness levels of 10, 50 and 100 percent and smooth stepless dimming between 10 and 100 percent, with a memory function so it returns to your last setting. A frosted lens is said to reduce glare by 70 percent, which is welcome on glossy pages.

The listing mentions three color temperatures but the snippet does not list the exact Kelvin values, so check the product page if you need a specific amber. More control also means more buttons to press, and a frosted lens softens the beam but can reduce throw for people who like a tight spotlight.

USB C charging means one cable for your phone and your light, and runtime depends on brightness level. Wipe the lens with a soft cloth when it gets dusty. Next to the Gritin 19 LED it offers smoother dimming, while against the Amber Light + it offers color choice instead of a single warm tone.
products.bestFor: People who want smooth control over brightness and softer, glare reduced light.
pros: Memory function returns to your last setting
cons: Exact color temperature values are not listed
Frosted lens gives a softer beam, not a tight spot

products.name: Amber Light + Rechargeable Amber Book Light
products.description:
The Amber Light + is a single color book light and does that one job better than the multi color options. Its 1600K amber glow is the warmest in this guide, and the listing says it blocks 99.95 percent of blue light, which suits late night reading when you do not want to wake your brain. Three brightness settings of 25, 50 and 100 percent give 20, 40 and 80 lumens.

The limit is flexibility. You get only amber, so it is a poor choice for daytime reading or for colored artwork in a book. At 80 lumens on the highest setting it is also brighter than the 15 to 50 lumens usually enough for close page reading, so the lower settings will do most of the work.

A 1000 mAh lithium battery gives 30 plus hours, and you charge it by USB. It clips on and is giftable. Compared with the DEWENWILS it is warmer at 1600K versus 1800K, and against the Gritin 19 LED it trades color choice for a purer amber.
products.bestFor: Night readers who want the warmest, most blue light free glow.
pros: 1600K amber is the warmest option here
Three clear levels of 20, 40 and 80 lumens
cons: Amber only, not ideal for daytime reading
Highest setting is brighter than most pages need

products.name: Gritin Eye Caring Neck Book Light with Timer
products.description:
This Gritin is a neck light, which means it hangs around your shoulders and leaves both hands free. It offers four color temperatures starting at amber 2000K, five brightness levels or stepless dimming, and a 30 minute timer that shuts the light off after you drift to sleep. The listing says it makes a circle of light that does not disturb a sleeping partner.

A neck light is bulkier than a clip and less portable, and some people find wearing one for an hour more tiring than clipping a light to a page. Its warmest setting at 2000K is slightly less warm than the 1600K and 1800K single color options, and the light is aimed at your lap rather than a page that you hold up.

A 1000 mAh battery is said to run 80 plus hours depending on brightness, and it charges by USB C. Next to the Gritin 19 LED it frees your hands but is bigger, and against the DEWENWILS it offers many more settings. If you want one light that stays on you through reading, a crossword and a podcast, this is the easiest of the group to live with.
products.bestFor: Readers who want hands free light with a sleep timer for a shared bedroom.
pros: Four color temperatures with stepless dimming
cons: Bulkier and less portable than a clip
Warmest setting is 2000K, not as warm as the amber pick

products.name: HEMONNKAM Rechargeable Clip On Book Light
products.description:
The HEMONNKAM is a straightforward clip on light with five brightness levels and three color modes. Its warmest setting is 3000K, which is the top of the amber range commonly suggested for bedtime reading, and it also offers 4500K and 6000K for daytime. A 500 mAh battery runs from 8 to 80 hours depending on the brightness.

Its amber is less warm than the 1600K and 1800K dedicated amber lights, so night readers who want the least blue light should look elsewhere. The battery is half the size of the 1000 mAh models, and the 8 hour figure at the high end means you may charge more often than with the Gritin or Amber Light +.

It does a basic job without fuss: clip, choose a color, adjust and read. Charging by USB takes a short time. Against the Gritin 19 LED it has a smaller battery and a less warm amber, while compared with the 86lux it gives step brightness instead of smooth dimming.
products.bestFor: Everyday readers who want a simple clip light with a few color choices.
pros: Five brightness levels for fine adjustment
Rechargeable with a runtime up to 80 hours
cons: Warmest setting is 3000K, less warm than amber lights
500 mAh battery means more frequent charging

products.name: DEWENWILS Amber Warm Clip On Book Reading Light

specList.label: Charging
specList.value: 1.5 hours for about 8 hours of use, built in USB

products.description:
The DEWENWILS is a no fuss amber light with a single color, three brightness levels, and a built in USB plug. At 1800K it blocks 99.95 percent of blue light, according to the listing, so it will not stimulate your eyes before sleep. One tap cycles through 30, 60 and 100 percent brightness.

Its battery gives about 8 hours after 1.5 hours of charging, which is shorter than the 30 plus and 80 plus hour figures on the other lights here. It has one color, so it is a poor daytime light, and the three brightness steps are fewer than on the Gritin or 86lux.

The built in USB means you plug the light directly into a charger without a cable, which is convenient but means you need a nearby port. Compared with the Amber Light + it is slightly less warm at 1800K versus 1600K, and against the HEMONNKAM it offers a warmer, simpler single mode. It is the easiest light in this guide to explain to someone who just wants it to work.
products.bestFor: Night readers who want a simple amber light with one tap brightness.
pros: One tap cycles three brightness levels
Built in USB plug needs no cable
cons: About 8 hours per charge is shorter than the others

buyingCriteria.explanation: Warm amber, about 1800K to 3200K, is generally recommended for bedtime reading, while 5000K to 6000K suits daytime focus. The Amber Light + at 1600K and the DEWENWILS at 1800K are warmest, the HEMONNKAM starts at 3000K, and the Gritin 19 LED spans 1800K to 6000K. If you read only at night, a single amber light is fine. If you read at all hours, pick a multi color model.

For close page reading, roughly 15 to 50 lumens is usually enough, and very high output only causes glare on white paper. The Amber Light + gives 20, 40 and 80 lumens, and the 86lux dims smoothly from 10 to 100 percent with a frosted lens said to reduce glare by 70 percent. Choose a light with a low setting, since most reading happens there.

Runtime drops sharply at the highest brightness, so compare figures at a stated level. The Gritin neck light and 19 LED have 1000 mAh batteries for up to 80 hours at the lowest setting, while the HEMONNKAM has 500 mAh for 8 to 80 hours and the DEWENWILS runs about 8 hours per charge. A larger battery means fewer chargings.

A neck light makes a light bubble for you without disturbing others, but is bulkier and less portable than a clip. The Gritin neck light is the neck pick, and the other five clip on. A good clip does not flop over when you turn the page. Choose a neck light if you hold books awkwardly or lie flat.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Controls you can use in the dark
buyingCriteria.explanation: More modes mean more button presses. The DEWENWILS needs one tap to change brightness, while the Gritin 19 LED and 86lux add color buttons and dimming. A memory function, as on the 86lux, returns to your last setting, saving presses. Pick the simplest control scheme you will actually use.

USB C is now standard and reversible, which is easier to plug in at night. The 86lux and Gritin neck light use USB C, and the DEWENWILS has a built in USB plug with no cable. A built in plug is handy but needs a port within reach. Check which cable you own before buying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Color and warmth
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared color temperature ranges from the product specs. The Amber Light + at 1600K is the warmest and the HEMONNKAM at 3000K is the least warm among the amber options. We favored lights that offer a true amber and, if multi color, a wide range.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brightness control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the number of brightness levels and whether dimming is stepless. The 86lux's 10 to 100 percent stepless dimming scored best, while the DEWENWILS with three steps is the most basic. We valued a low setting suited to close reading.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery life
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated runtimes and battery capacity. The Gritin 19 LED and neck light at 1000 mAh and 80 plus hours lead, while the DEWENWILS at about 8 hours trails. We noted that runtimes vary with brightness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Form and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered clip versus neck designs, head width and aiming. The Gritin 19 LED's wide head and gooseneck scored well, and the neck light adds hands free use. We looked at weight and bulk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed how many presses it takes to get the light you want. One tap on the DEWENWILS is simplest, and memory on the 86lux helps. We favored controls that work with sleepy fingers.

cards.label: Clip on
cards.text: A clip light lights the page and stays small. The Gritin 19 LED, 86lux, Amber Light +, HEMONNKAM and DEWENWILS are clip ons. They need a book or e reader to clip to. Choose a clip if you travel or read in bed with a book.

cards.label: Neck light
cards.text: A neck light hangs on your shoulders and frees your hands. The Gritin neck light is the neck pick. It is bulkier. Choose a neck light for knitting, magazines or reading while lying down.

howToChoose.note: Most readers do well with a clip, such as the Gritin 19 LED.

faq.q: How do I choose between amber and multi color lights?
faq.a: Choose amber like the Amber Light + or DEWENWILS if you read only at night. Choose a multi color light like the Gritin 19 LED if you read at different times. Amber at 1800K or warmer suits bedtime.

faq.q: How much does a good book light cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely, but features rather than cost decide value. Look for a warm setting, a low brightness level and USB C or USB charging. Spend more for fine dimming and bigger batteries.

faq.q: How long should the battery last?
faq.a: Runtimes depend on brightness. The Gritin lights list 80 plus hours at the lowest setting, while the DEWENWILS runs about 8 hours per charge. Charge weekly if you read nightly.

faq.q: Is amber light really better at night?
faq.a: Warm amber, around 1800K to 3200K, is generally recommended for bedtime reading because it has less blue light. Claims like blocking 99.95 percent are manufacturer statements. Adjust brightness low as well.

faq.q: How bright should a book light be?
faq.a: About 15 to 50 lumens is usually enough for close reading, and more causes glare. The Amber Light + gives 20, 40 and 80 lumens. Use the lower settings.

faq.q: Will a clip light damage my book?
faq.a: A padded clip is gentle on pages and covers. Choose one that does not flop when you turn the page. Clip it to the cover and not to thin pages.

faq.q: Do I need a neck light?
faq.a: A neck light such as the Gritin is useful for hands free reading and for partner friendly beams. A clip is smaller and easier to travel with.
